descriptions.value: vault-java-driver, a Java client for HashiCorp Vault, silently disables TLS certificate and hostname verification in three states where the caller asked for verification: an SslConfig passed to VaultConfig without calling build(), an SslConfig restored by Java deserialization, and VAULT_SSL_VERIFY set to a truthy value other than "true", such as 1, yes or on. In each case SslConfig.isVerify() returns false and the driver installs a trust-all SSLContext. An attacker on the network path to the Vault server can then read the Vault token and secrets in transit and forge responses. This issue affects io.github.jopenlibs:vault-java-driver 5.2.0 through 6.2.3. It is fixed in 7.0.0.

vault-java-driver, a Java client for HashiCorp Vault, parses Vault's JSON responses with a vendored minimal-json parser that has no nesting depth limit. A deeply nested value raises a StackOverflowError, which escapes catch (Exception) handlers and kills the reading thread. A Vault token that can write but not read a KV v2 path can store such a value there, so every later read of that path through the driver fails. This requires Vault 1.19.x or earlier, because 1.20 and later reject values nested deeper than 298 levels. This issue affects io.github.jopenlibs:vault-java-driver 5.2.0 through 6.2.3 and is fixed in 7.0.0.

Agenta before 0.122.5 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability that allows workspace members with workflow edit rights to redirect workflow invocations by setting arbitrary revision URLs. Attackers can capture the attached secret-resolve Authorization token to read provider secrets from the vault API, or reach internal and cloud metadata addresses.

OS command injection in the pass and bitwarden credential providers in Eclipse Foundation Eclipse Otterdog through 1.7.1 allows a user able to modify an organization configuration to execute arbitrary commands with the privileges of the operator running otterdog, including access to their credential vault, via a crafted secret reference (pass:<path> or bitwarden:<item>@<field>) or credential identifier that is resolved when otterdog apply is run.

Improper access control in the administrative role assignment endpoint in Devolutions Server 2026.3.13.0 and earlier allows an authenticated user with only vault assignment management rights to escalate privileges and read vault entry passwords via a crafted role assignment request.

Improper access control in the autofill vault search in Devolutions Server 2026.3.13.0 and earlier allows an authenticated user with only view permission on a shared entry to obtain its password in clear text via a linked credential entry created in their private vault.

HashiCorp Vault and Vault Enterprise are vulnerable to an issue in the integrated storage join process that may allow an unauthenticated attacker with network access to a new, uninitialized node to cause that node to send credentials from its server environment to an attacker-controlled server. This vulnerability (CVE-2026-92735) is fixed in Vault Community Edition 2.2.2 and Vault Enterprise 2.2.2, 1.21.14, and 1.19.25.

Vault's audit devices did not validate the contents of a configured audit log prefix and did not consistently enforce the server-level setting that restricts audit log prefixing. This may allow a privileged operator to inject content into audit logs, potentially leading to forged or misleading audit records. This vulnerability (CVE-2026-93333) is fixed in Vault Community Edition 2.2.2 and Vault Enterprise 2.2.2, 1.21.14, and 1.19.25.

Vault Community Edition and Vault Enterprise did not consistently apply explicit ACL policy deny rules to request paths that differ only by a trailing slash. This may allow an authenticated user who holds a broader delete permission on system configuration paths to disable a secrets engine, auth method, or audit device that a more specific deny rule was intended to protect. This vulnerability (CVE-2026-93335) is fixed in Vault Community Edition 2.2.2 and Vault Enterprise 2.2.2, 1.21.14, and 1.19.25.

Vault Community Edition and Vault Enterprise did not apply explicit ACL policy deny rules to letter case variants of user and group names in auth methods that treat these names as case-insensitive. This may allow an authenticated user with delegated permissions to modify a protected user or group, potentially leading to privilege escalation. This vulnerability (CVE-2026-128100) is fixed in Vault Community Edition 2.2.2 and Vault Enterprise 2.2.2, 1.21.14, and 1.19.25.

Vault's Login MFA feature did not consistently enforce the lifetime of pending two-phase login requests. This may allow a user who previously completed the first authentication factor to complete MFA and obtain a Vault token after the pending request should have expired, including after the user's primary credential has been rotated. This vulnerability (CVE-2026-92738) is fixed in Vault Community Edition 2.2.2 and Vault Enterprise 2.2.2, 1.21.14, and 1.19.26.

Zyrabit Platform provides sovereign AI infrastructure for enterprise retrieval-augmented generation. Prior to 2.4.4, import_to_vault(source_path, destination_name) accepts both caller-controlled paths, but the content-pattern guard does not confine destination_name. The vulnerable tool is implemented in zyrabit-slm/api-rag/app/domain/services/mcp_service.py, where Path(DOCS_DIR) / destination_name is passed to shutil.copy2, allowing traversal or an absolute destination to write outside the vault. An unrestricted source_path can be copied into the vault and retrieved through secure_query, disclosing files readable by the service; files that do not match the executable-pattern filter pass that filter. When ENABLE_LEGACY_EXTENSIONS=true, zyrabit-slm/api-rag/app/main.py registers POST /mcp/rpc without get_current_user, allowing unauthenticated network tool calls; this optional exposure is disabled by default and is not required for local invocation. If an attacker can stage chosen source content and write to an execution-triggered destination, the advisory describes conditional process execution. This issue is fixed in version 2.4.4.

obsidian-sync-mcp is an MCP server that gives AI agents access to Obsidian vaults. Prior to 0.5.7, deployments running without MCP_AUTH_TOKEN install no serverOptions.authenticate check for the HTTP /mcp endpoint, so requests are dispatched without validating the Host or Origin headers. A malicious website visited by the operator can use DNS rebinding to reach loopback, LAN, VPN, or container-published addresses, or directly issue a cross-origin request to loopback, and invoke the MCP tool surface to read, create, overwrite, delete, or move vault notes. Deployments using MCP_AUTH_TOKEN are not affected because browsers do not attach the bearer token. This issue is fixed in version 0.5.7.
In JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.2.2 missing authorization allowed project developers to read arbitrary HashiCorp Vault secrets

mcp-ssh-manager is an MCP server for managing servers over SSH with human approval, an encrypted vault, and a live audit trail. Prior to 3.8.5, ssh_backup_create, ssh_backup_restore, ssh_backup_schedule, and ssh_backup_list build remote shell commands from caller-controlled values in src/backup-manager.js and inline backup handlers in src/index.js without neutralizing shell metacharacters. Crafted database, connection, backup directory, path, exclusion, schedule, or comment arguments can therefore execute arbitrary OS commands on managed remote servers as the configured SSH user. ssh_backup_schedule can persist execution through cron. ssh_backup_list does not pass through the server policy check and remains available in readonly and restricted modes, allowing command execution despite those restrictions. Tool arguments can be supplied by a malicious or compromised MCP client or steered through indirect prompt injection; fully trusted benign arguments do not trigger the issue. The earlier database-helper remediation for CVE-2026-77383 applied shell quoting to src/database-manager.js but did not cover these parallel backup builders. This issue is fixed in version 3.8.5.

mcp-ssh-manager is an MCP server for managing servers over SSH with human approval, an encrypted vault, and a live audit trail. Prior to 3.6.7, ssh_db_list, ssh_db_dump, ssh_db_import, and ssh_db_restore in src/database-manager.js interpolate caller-controlled database, table, collection, file path, user, host, port, and password values into shell-evaluated command strings without neutralization. Shell metacharacters in these arguments therefore execute arbitrary commands on the configured SSH target as the account used by the MCP server. ssh_db_list is classified as read-only and remains available in readonly and restricted server security modes, so this path bypasses the command-execution boundary those modes are intended to enforce. The dump and import builders are blocked in readonly mode but remain vulnerable in the default unrestricted mode. The earlier version 3.6.5 hardening covered only ssh_db_query query text; it did not protect the list, dump, import, or restore builders, or the connection flags used by query builders. This issue is fixed in version 3.6.7.

Authorization bypass through user-controlled key in the RDM folder duplication endpoint in Devolutions Server 2026.3.14.0 and earlier allows an authenticated low-privileged attacker to overwrite and move arbitrary vault entries and read their history via a client-supplied entry identifier.

Improper access control in the repository access request endpoint in Devolutions Server 2026.3.14.0 and earlier allows an authenticated low-privileged user to self-approve an access request via an out-of-range vault type value that skips the approval check.

Use of a default cryptographic key in the instance registration component in Amazon SSM Agent before 3.3.5226.0 on AWS-provided Windows Server AMIs released before 2026-09-09 might allow local users without administrative privileges to obtain the instance's Default Host Management Configuration role credentials via the registration key shared by all instances launched from the same AMI.



To remediate this issue, users should replace affected instances with instances launched from AWS Windows Server AMIs released on or after 2026-09-09, which include SSM Agent 3.3.5226.0 or later. Upgrading the agent in place does not replace the shared key, and deleting the agent's Vault breaks instances managed through Default Host Management Configuration.
